name: Introductory Biology
backbone_line: The backbone of this course is MIT OpenCourseWare 7.016 Introductory Biology (Fall 2018, Prof. Barbara Imperiali and Prof. Adam Martin) and 7.012 Introduction to Biology (Fall 2004, Prof. Eric Lander, Prof. Robert Weinberg, and colleagues), published under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike licence. The wording of this Brief course is original to the Academy.
formula_phrase: write the actual chemical and biological notation: base-pairing rules, codons, Punnett squares, the overall equations of respiration and photosynthesis, and simple genetic ratios such as 3:1 and 9:3:3:1
drawings: a DNA double helix, a folded protein, a eukaryotic cell with its organelles, a mitochondrion with ATP synthase, pea plants with purple and white flowers, chromosomes during meiosis, a ribosome reading mRNA, a PCR tube in a thermal cycler, an antibody binding a virus, a branching tree of life, a handwritten diagram with a genuine pencil-and-paper look
names_example: ENGR 506 B, MIT 7.016, MIT 7.012, the central dogma, CRISPR-Cas9, the lac operon, Mendel's laws

- ENGR 500 B, How to Use the Engineering Courses, is Course Zero for the Engineering library.
